proposal.summary: The requester (SH-CS, CL-01) asked for an AI agent to auto-answer disputes and auto-fix wrong bills, framing the Aug-Sep ticket surge (610→1180→1260/month, E-03) as a response-handling problem. Investigation rejected that framing (response times are within SLA, E-02) and, after an evidence-driven reframe (dependency review DR-1 triggered by E-12), established the confirmed root problem as PD-1@v2: billing rule BV-17 (deployed 2026-08-01, E-13) compares raw AMI register values to 12-month m3 history without unit scaling, and firmware v4.2 meters (E-14) report in 0.1 m3 units, so 1184 of 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputed bills (95.5%) had a genuine timely AMI read wrongly rejected (E-12). Field staffing shortfall (E-01, E-06) and tariff change (E-05, E-07) were examined and found not to be the driver. The DEFINE gate reached CONDITIONAL_PASS. Because no automated bill writes are allowed (K-BILLWRITE) and the root-cause fix is not executable within this agent's authority, the released agent (SD-2) is limited to two read-only monitoring deliverables - query_billing_rule_change_log (DA-RULES) and monitor_dispute_volume_trend (DA-TICKET) - not the originally requested auto-fix/auto-answer capability. The release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION with no holds, reflecting that the mechanism is confirmed and no protected action was taken, but several verification obligations and the real fix remain outstanding.
